name: DEAD LEDGER
description: A purely analog debt-and-death bluffing card game played with a 54-card hand-printed deck, popular in Shelf bars and back-room establishments where connectivity is either unavailable or deliberately blocked. Players represent creditors collecting from a deceased debtor's estate, lying and counter-lying about what they are owed, with the pot going to whoever holds the final valid claim. The cards are deliberately crude — block-printed on recycled stock — and counterfeiting them is considered a local art form.
story_hooks: A real creditor starts showing up at Shelf bars where Dead Ledger is played, using the game's social networks to identify debtors.
A particular hand-printed deck begins circulating that contains actual account numbers and debt records hidden in the card art.
A player wins every session for months — locals suspect a BCI exploit, but the player claims to be entirely unaugmented.
